# Markdown Documentation Instructions
applyTo: "**/*.md"

## Documentation Standards
- Use clear, descriptive headings with proper hierarchy
- Write content in Portuguese for this learning project
- Include code examples with proper syntax highlighting
- Use consistent formatting for links and references

## Structure Guidelines
- Start with a clear title (# Level 1 heading)
- Use level 2 headings (##) for main sections
- Keep paragraphs concise and focused
- Use lists for step-by-step instructions

## Code Examples
- Always specify language in code blocks (```javascript, ```html, etc.)
- Include complete, working examples when possible
- Add comments in code examples to explain key concepts
- Use consistent indentation in code blocks

## Links and References
- Use descriptive link text instead of "click here"
- Include links to official documentation when referencing tools
- Use relative links for internal project files
- Test all external links periodically

## Learning Notes Format
- Use bullet points for key concepts
- Include practical examples alongside theory
- Add "⚠️" for important warnings or gotchas
- Use "💡" for tips and best practices

## GitHub Copilot Documentation
- Document commands clearly (/init, /instructions, etc.)
- Include screenshots when they add value
- Explain the purpose and context of each feature
- Provide step-by-step tutorials for complex features

## Formatting
- Use **bold** for important terms and concepts
- Use `inline code` for commands, file names, and code snippets
- Use > blockquotes for important notes or quotes
- Maintain consistent spacing between sections
